subject: ARTHIST
course_description: Special topics in Art History. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.
course_notes: (Same as CHN 375 2) Brought to ancient China by travelling merchants and monks, Buddhism was once a foreign religion. Yet not long after the initial introduction, Buddhist art and monuments flourished and gradually became a part of Chinese visual culture. At times, Buddhist art helped to build a cosmopolitan society that encouraged foreign trade. In other times, painting Buddhist subjects and visiting ancient Buddhist sites were high-minded pursuits of educated Chinese elites. Women from different social classes also found motivations to participate in the making and collecting of Buddhist art and materials. This course explores grandiose sculptures, mural paintings, cliff-carved cave-shrines, paintings, prints, and textiles in Chinese Buddhist visual culture. We will address how issues of politics, patronage, gender, and economy shaped the production and reception of Chinese Buddhist art. Art History major/minor: Division II or IV
